Sound good if I ask you some questions while you keep browsing?
Yep, go for it — ask away.
Alright, let's start with the pain point you mentioned. You mentioned the sagging in the middle like a hammock—what else about your current setup bothers you the most?

Shallow depth and dog hair magnet—those are real frustrations. How does the shallow depth affect movie nights and lounging for you?
I end up half-hanging off it trying to nap — my golden retriever gets more of the couch than I do.
Half hanging off trying to nap—that's the worst. What do you definitely not want to repeat with the next couch?
No more shallow seats or fabric that clings to dog hair — I want deep and durable.
Deep seats and something that doesn't trap every hair—smart priorities. If you got the next couch exactly right, what would be different about how you use the living room?
I'd actually nap on it instead of the floor, and we'd host movie nights more often.

Napping on the couch instead of the floor and more movie nights—that's a great outcome to aim for. What would the ideal couch feel like when you sit or lie on it—deep and sink-in, more supportive, or somewhere in between?
Somewhere in between — sink-in enough to nap, but I don't want to need a crane to get out of it.
Got it—sink-in for naps but easy to get out of. Anything else you're picturing about the look or feel of the finished room?
Something warm and modern — maybe a mid-tone gray or greige, nothing too fussy.
Warm modern with a mid-tone gray or beige—sounds like a clean, inviting vibe. When are you hoping to have the new couch in place?
Ideally within the next month or so — before the holidays hit.
Is there a move, event, family visit, or anything else you're trying to have the room ready for?
Yeah, my in-laws visit over Thanksgiving, so I'd love it done before then.

Thanksgiving in-laws—that's a solid reason to move on this. Before we look at anything, let's lock in what this couch absolutely has to get right. Based on everything we've talked about, what would you say are the two or three things it has to nail?
Deep enough to nap on, pet-hair-friendly durable fabric, and comfortably seats four.
Are there any dealbreakers where even if you loved how it looked, you wouldn't buy it?
Yeah — anything white, or a fabric that needs professional cleaning.
White or high-maintenance fabrics are out—smart call with the golden. Is there a maximum size we absolutely can't go past, or a doorway it has to fit through?
The wall's about 9 feet, and our front door is a standard 32-inch one.
Nine-foot wall and a 32-inch door—plenty to work with. What's the total price range you're hoping to stay around—comfortable target or hard maximum?
Comfortable target is around $1,500, but I could stretch to $2,000 for the right one.

riley.quinn88@gmail.com — that's the best one.
Anything important about the couch, the room, or what matters to you that we haven't talked about yet?
Oh — we've got a toddler too, so bonus points if it survives juice spills.
